content.title: Coachella 2026 Weekend 2 | Full Festival Guide
content.text: Source: ChatGpt Weekend 1 of Coachella 2026 (April 10–12) in Indio, California wrapped up on a high note. Travis Scott opened Friday with a high-energy set packed with pyrotechnics, while Beyoncé closed Saturday night with a show full of jaw-dropping visuals and surprise guest appearances. Dua Lipa closed out Sunday with a crowd-pleasing mix of hits that had everyone dancing. On the smaller stages, rising stars like Rina Sawayama, PinkPantheress, and Fred again.. stole the spotlight, while spontaneous pop-up sets kept fans on their toes. Meanwhile, immersive art installations and interactive experiences at DoLaB gave attendees plenty to explore beyond the music. With sunny days reaching 95°F (35°C), the festival grounds were alive with energy, setting a high bar for Weekend 2. Get ready for Coachella 2026 Weekend 2 with everything you need to know before you go. This guide covers standout artists, stage layouts, set times, and practical tips for handling crowds, food, and desert heat so you can move through the festival smoothly and make the most of every set. Artists to Watch at Coachella 2026 (Weekend 2) Weekend 2 of Coachella 2026 brings back the big names, with Travis Scott, Beyoncé, and Dua Lipa all returning to the Main Stage. Expect the same full production setups, packed crowds, and hit-heavy sets that made Weekend 1 so talked about. Over at the Sahara Tent, Fred again.. stands out with his live-style electronic set that blends DJing with real-time sampling, giving it more of a concert feel than a traditional DJ performance. On the Outdoor Theatre stage, Rina Sawayama delivers a genre-blending set that moves between pop, rock, and experimental sounds, while PinkPantheress keeps things light, fast, and catchy with her signature short-form, internet-era pop tracks. Stages and Daily Schedule Weekend 2 of Coachella 2026, happening April 17–19, follows the same overall flow as the first weekend. Music usually kicks off around 1:00 PM PT and runs until about 1:00 AM on Friday and Saturday, with Sunday wrapping up closer to midnight. The festival is spread across seven main stages, each with its own vibe and crowd. Festival Map and Stage Layout: Source: ChatGpt The Coachella grounds in Indio are massive, set across an open desert field, so getting around takes time and a bit of planning. Here’s how the main stages break down: Coachella Stage (Main Stage): The biggest stage, where headliners and closing sets take place Outdoor Theatre: A large secondary stage for major acts and strong counter-programming Sahara Tent: High-energy electronic, hip-hop, and pop with heavy production Mojave Stage: Mid-size tent for indie, alternative, and crossover artists Gobi Stage: Smaller stage focused on emerging and global acts Sonora Stage: Dedicated to punk, rock, and underground sounds Quasar / Do LaB: Known for DJ sets, experimental performances, and surprise guests One thing to keep in mind for Weekend 2 is distance. The Sahara Tent is quite far from the Main Stage, and getting between them can take 10 to 20 minutes, especially at night when crowds are at their peak. Set Times and Daily Flow: Set times can shift slightly for Weekend 2, but the overall rhythm of the day remains consistent: Afternoon (1:00 PM – 4:00 PM): Early sets from up-and-coming artists on Sonora, Gobi, and Mojave Late Afternoon (4:00 PM – 7:00 PM): Mid-level acts fill out Outdoor Theatre, Sahara, and Mojave Evening (7:00 PM – 9:00 PM): Bigger names and popular acts draw heavier crowds Night (9:00 PM – close): Headliners take over the Main Stage Most headliners go on between 9:00 PM and midnight, with Sunday ending a little earlier due to curfew. Conclusion Weekend 2 of Coachella 2026 is all about having a plan while staying flexible. Lock in your must-see sets like Beyoncé, Travis Scott, and Dua Lipa, share your schedule with your group, and pick a meetup spot in case service drops. Keep checking the official Coachella app for real-time updates, since set times and surprise performances can change. Most importantly, enjoy the experience, explore beyond the main stages, and take in everything the festival has to offer. This guide is presented by IndianEagle, offering deals on flights between the USA and India for travelers planning seamless international journeys. FAQs When is Coachella 2026 Weekend 2? Coachella 2026 Weekend 2 is scheduled for April 17–19, 2026, in Indio, California. What time does Coachella usually start and end each day? Most days start around 1:00 PM PT. Music typically runs until around 1:00 AM on Friday and Saturday, and until midnight on Sunday. Do Weekend 1 and Weekend 2 have the same lineup? Yes, the lineup is mostly the same, including headliners like Beyoncé, Travis Scott, and Dua Lipa, though there may be small schedule changes or surprise guests. How long does it take to walk between stages? Walking between major stages, especially between the Sahara Tent and Main Stage, can take about 10 to 20 minutes depending on crowd flow. What should I bring to Coachella Weekend 2? Essentials include a refillable water bottle, sunscreen, comfortable shoes, sunglasses, a hat, and a portable phone charger.
